turns.prompt:
You are given an attached CSV file b3_supercon_target.csv: 229 real samples,
column `composition` (element fractions as a compact formula string) and
column `target` (the measured critical temperature Tc (K)).

Propose a composition — a value for each element fraction below, within each
observed range, whose critical temperature Tc (K) is AS CLOSE AS POSSIBLE to
90. Design variables:
  - O (fraction in [0, 0.697674])
  - Cu (fraction in [0, 0.454545])
  - Ba (fraction in [0, 0.333333])
  - Sr (fraction in [0, 0.285714])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.

turns.answer_text:
The provided samples include many compositions whose elemental makeup is restricted to the 20 allowed design variables. Among those valid samples the measured Tc values nearest 90 K are 67 K (a heavily substituted Y/Ca/Ba/La cuprate) and 110 K (Bi2Sr2CaCu2O10). The latter lies closer (absolute error 20 K versus 23 K).  

All other high-Tc entries either contain disallowed elements (Tl, Hg, Mg, rare earths, \ldots) or lie farther from the target. Consequently the atomic fractions of the 110 K Bi-2212/2223-type phase are adopted directly (coefficients summed to 17 atoms, then normalized). Every coordinate remains inside the observed box and the unused design variables are set to zero.
